knowledge_statements.title: Process-Level Tightness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-containment and modulus criterion for tightness of continuous stochastic processes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^n\) be random elements of \(C([0,T];\mathbb R^d)\), and define \(w_T(x,\delta)=\sup\{\|x(t)-x(s)\|:0\le s,t\le T,\ |t-s|\le\delta\}\). The family \(\{X^n\}\) is tight if, for every \(\eta>0\), there is \(K<\infty\) with \(\sup_n\mathbb P(\sup_{t\le T}\|X^n(t)\|>K)<\eta\), and \(\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\sup_n\mathbb P(w_T(X^n,\delta)>\eta)=0\). If these conditions hold for every \(T>0\), the laws are tight in the locally uniform continuous-path space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact containment and uniformly vanishing path oscillations imply tightness of the process laws on continuous-path space.

knowledge_statements.title: Subsequence Limit Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification of weak subsequential limits by integral equations or martingale problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(X^n\) is tight in a Polish path space. For each subsequence choose a further subsequence with \(X^{n_j}\Rightarrow X\). knowledge_statements.title: Convergence-Rate Results
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root-mean-square iteration rate derived from bounded normalized stochastic-approximation errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_n\) converge to \(x^*\), and suppose the normalized errors \(Z_n=\sqrt n(x_n-x^*)\) satisfy \(\sup_n\mathbb E\|Z_n\|^2<C\). Then \(\mathbb E\|x_n-x^*\|^2\le C/n\), so the root-mean-square error is at most \(\sqrt{C/n}\). Consequently, in the one-simulation-oracle-call-per-iteration model, achieving \((\mathbb E\|x_n-x^*\|^2)^{1/2}\le\varepsilon\) requires at most \(N(\varepsilon)=\lceil C\varepsilon^{-2}\rceil\) iterations and oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded root-n normalized errors give mean-square rate O(1/n) and RMS oracle complexity O(epsilon to the minus two).

children.title: Unstable-Limit Avoidance
children.top_down_role: Results concerning avoidance of repelling or otherwise unstable limiting states.

knowledge_statements.title: Unstable-Limit Avoidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvergence to a linearly unstable equilibrium of a smooth stochastic-approximation mean flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{n+1}=x_n+a_n(h(x_n)+M_{n+1}+r_n)\), and let \(x^u\) satisfy \(h(x^u)=0\). Assume \(h\) is continuously differentiable near \(x^u\), its Jacobian \(Dh(x^u)\) has an eigenvalue with positive real part, the gains satisfy \(\sum_n a_n=\infty\) and \(\sum_n a_n^2<\infty\), and \(r_n\) is asymptotically negligible. If the martingale noise has bounded conditional second moments and uniformly nonzero conditional variance on the unstable subspace near \(x^u\), then \(\mathbb P(x_n\to x^u)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic approximation cannot converge with positive probability to a linearly unstable equilibrium when noise persistently excites its unstable subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is continuously differentiable and \(Dh(x^u)\) has an eigenvalue with positive real part
\(\sum_n a_n=\infty\), \(\sum_n a_n^2<\infty\), and the remainder is negligible
The martingale noise persistently excites the unstable subspace
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\lim_{n\to\infty}x_n=x^u)=0\)

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the mean drift at the equilibrium

children.title: Polyak-Ruppert Averaging
children.top_down_role: Averaged-recursion families for stability and asymptotic efficiency.

children.title: Full-History Averaging
children.top_down_role: Averaging over the expanding recursion history.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-History Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyak–Ruppert averaging over all iterates produced after initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given iterates \(x_{n+1}=x_n+a_nY_{n+1}\) in \(\mathbb R^d\), initialize \(S_1=x_1\) and \(\bar x_1=x_1\). For \(n\ge2\), after computing \(x_n\), update \(S_n=S_{n-1}+x_n\) and \(\bar x_n=S_n/n\), equivalently \(\bar x_n=\bar x_{n-1}+(x_n-\bar x_{n-1})/n\). Stop according to a prescribed iteration budget or diagnostic and return \(\bar x_n=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^n x_k\), rather than the final raw iterate \(x_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain the running arithmetic mean of every recursion iterate and return that mean when the stopping rule triggers.
assumptions_latex: An initial iterate \(x_1\in\mathbb R^d\) is given
The base recursion supplies each subsequent iterate \(x_n\)
A stopping budget or diagnostic is specified
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x_n=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n x_k\) is the algorithm output

notation.meaning: running sum of all iterates through n

children.title: Window-Limited Averaging
children.top_down_role: Averages formed from bounded or moving portions of the recursion history.

knowledge_statements.title: Window-Limited Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform averaging over a moving, finite suffix of stochastic-approximation iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x_k)_{k\geq 1}\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), and let \((m_n)_{n\geq1}\) satisfy \(1\leq m_n\leq n\). The window-limited average at time \(n\) is
\[\bar x_n^{(m)}=\frac{1}{m_n}\sum_{k=n-m_n+1}^{n}x_k.\]
Thus only the most recent \(m_n\) iterates contribute, each with weight \(m_n^{-1}\); observations preceding index \(n-m_n+1\) receive zero weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The estimator is the arithmetic mean of the most recent m_n iterates, excluding all earlier iterates.
assumptions_latex: \((x_k)_{k\geq1}\subset\mathbb{R}^d\)
\(1\leq m_n\leq n\)

notation.meaning: number of retained iterates at time n

children.title: Tail-Only Averaging
children.top_down_role: Averages that discard an initial recursion segment.

knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Only Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A suffix average obtained after discarding an initial burn-in segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For iterates \((x_k)_{k\geq1}\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), choose a burn-in index \(b_n\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\). The tail-only average is
\[\bar x_n^{\mathrm{tail}}=\frac{1}{n-b_n}\sum_{k=b_n+1}^{n}x_k.\]
Equivalently, it is window-limited averaging with window length \(m_n=n-b_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tail-only averaging discards the first b_n iterates and averages every iterate from b_n+1 through n.
assumptions_latex: \((x_k)_{k\geq1}\subset\mathbb{R}^d\)
\(0\leq b_n<n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x_n^{\mathrm{tail}}=(n-b_n)^{-1}\sum_{k=b_n+1}^{n}x_k\)

children.title: Window-Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Choices of averaging location and span relative to recursion length.

knowledge_statements.title: Window-Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic classification of averaging windows by their size relative to elapsed iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((m_n)_{n\geq1}\) be integers satisfying \(1\leq m_n\leq n\). A bounded-window regime satisfies \(\sup_n m_n<\infty\), while an expanding-window regime satisfies \(m_n\to\infty\). An expanding window is vanishing-fraction if \(m_n/n\to0\), fixed-fraction if \(m_n/n\to\rho\) for some \(\rho\in(0,1)\), and asymptotically full if \(m_n/n\to1\). If \(m_n/n\) has no limit, the expanding window belongs to none of these three limiting-fraction subclasses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Windows may be bounded or expanding. An expanding window is called vanishing-fraction, fixed-fraction, or asymptotically full when its retained fraction converges respectively to zero, a value strictly between zero and one, or one; a nonconvergent retained fraction is a separate residual case.
assumptions_latex: \(m_n\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) for every \(n\geq1\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_n m_n<\infty\), or \(m_n\to\infty\); in the latter case, when \(m_n/n\) converges, its limit lies in \([0,1]\) and determines the vanishing-fraction, fixed-fraction, or asymptotically full subclass

notation.meaning: limiting retained fraction strictly between zero and one

children.title: Averaging Efficiency Results
children.top_down_role: Efficiency and robustness consequences of iterate averaging.

knowledge_statements.title: Averaging Efficiency Results
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical Polyak–Ruppert central limit theorem for linearized stochastic approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(x_{n+1}=x_n-a_n(h(x_n)+\xi_{n+1})\) with \(a_n=n^{-\alpha}\), \(\alpha\in(1/2,1)\), and root \(h(x^*)=0\). Suppose \(x_n\to x^*\) in probability, \(h\) is differentiable at \(x^*\) with Hurwitz Jacobian \(H\), and \((\xi_{n+1})\) is a martingale-difference noise sequence whose conditional covariance converges to \(S\), under a uniform moment condition sufficient for the martingale central limit theorem. For \(\bar x_n=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^n x_k\),
\[\sqrt n(\bar x_n-x^*)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,H^{-1}SH^{-\mathsf T}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard local stability and martingale-noise conditions, full iterate averaging is asymptotically normal with the optimal linearized covariance.
assumptions_latex: \(a_n=n^{-\alpha}\) with \(1/2<\alpha<1\), and \(x_n\to x^*\) in probability
\(h(x^*)=0\), and \(H=Dh(x^*)\) is Hurwitz
\((\xi_{n+1})\) is martingale-difference noise with limiting conditional covariance \(S\) and suitable uniform moments
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sqrt n(\bar x_n-x^*)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,H^{-1}SH^{-\mathsf T})\)

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the mean field at the root

The vague moment and local-linearization hypotheses are also insufficient for a theorem record. The cited overview locator must be inspected for the exact theorem convention and assumptions.

children.title: Stochastic-Approximation Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural causes of divergence, stagnation, or unsuitable limits.

children.title: Recursion Containment Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Failure of recursion stability or containment.

children.title: Local Recursion Instability
children.top_down_role: Unstable behavior arising near candidate limiting states.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Recursion Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of Lyapunov stability near a mean-recursion equilibrium.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the deterministic stochastic-approximation skeleton \(x_{n+1}=x_n+a_n h(x_n)\), an equilibrium \(x^*\) is locally unstable if there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that, for every \(\delta>0\), some initialization with \(\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert<\delta\) has \(\lVert x_n-x^*\rVert\geq\varepsilon\) for some \(n\). For example, with \(h(x)=x\), \(a_n>0\), and \(\sum_n a_n=\infty\), every \(x_0\neq0\) satisfies \(|x_n|=|x_0|\prod_{k<n}(1+a_k)\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equilibrium is locally unstable when arbitrarily small perturbations eventually leave a fixed neighborhood; positive linear feedback gives a concrete example.
assumptions_latex: \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_n=\infty\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*=0\) is locally unstable for \(x_{n+1}=(1+a_n)x_n\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The instability definition and scalar example are mathematically plausible and fit the leaf, but no inspectable source supports this nontrivial failure-boundary record.

children.title: Divergent Iterates
children.top_down_role: Recursion paths that escape every bounded region.

knowledge_statements.title: Divergent Iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncontained stochastic recursion caused by nonvanishing noise increments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_0=0\) and \(x_{n+1}=x_n+\xi_{n+1}\), where \((\xi_n)\) are independent with \(\mathbb P(\xi_n=1)=\mathbb P(\xi_n=-1)=1/2\). This is a stochastic-approximation recursion with constant gain and zero mean field. The one-dimensional simple symmetric random walk is unbounded almost surely:
\[\mathbb P\!\left(\limsup_{n\to\infty}|x_n|=\infty\right)=1.\]
Hence unbiased noise alone does not ensure containment when its scaling does not decay.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant-gain recursion driven by unbiased signs is a random walk whose iterates are almost surely unbounded.
assumptions_latex: \((\xi_n)\) are independent symmetric random signs
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\limsup_{n\to\infty}|x_n|=\infty)=1\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The symmetric-random-walk counterexample is correct and appropriately typed, but the almost-sure unboundedness claim has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Transient Blow-Up
children.top_down_role: Large finite-time excursions that compromise estimation or numerical reliability.

knowledge_statements.title: Transient Blow-Up
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitrarily large finite excursions despite eventual recovery under a stable recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(a\in(0,1)\) and consider \(x_{n+1}=(1-a)x_n+a\xi_{n+1}\) with \(x_0=0\). For any prescribed \(M>0\), choose a disturbance sequence with \(\xi_1=M/a\) and \(\xi_n=0\) for \(n\geq2\). Then \(x_1=M\), while \(x_n=M(1-a)^{n-1}\to0\). Thus asymptotic stability does not provide a uniform finite-time bound when disturbances may have arbitrarily large magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single large disturbance can create any prescribed excursion even though the stable recursion subsequently converges back to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_1=M\) and \(x_n\to0\) for every prescribed \(M>0\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-excursion construction is internally correct and fits Transient Blow-Up, but it lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Persistent Estimator Bias
children.top_down_role: Systematic estimation error surviving recursion scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Estimator Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonvanishing mean estimation error shifts the limiting equilibrium.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x_{n+1}=x_n-a_n(x_n+b+\xi_{n+1})\), where \(b\neq0\), \(\sum_n a_n=\infty\), \(\sum_n a_n^2<\infty\), and \((\xi_{n+1})\) is martingale-difference noise with uniformly bounded conditional second moments. Under the usual boundedness condition for the recursion, \(x_n\to-b\) almost surely. The intended unbiased root is \(0\), so a bias that survives multiplication by the gain sequence changes the mean-field root and yields nonzero limiting error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant bias in the gradient estimator shifts the recursion’s limit from the intended root zero to minus the bias.
assumptions_latex: \(b\neq0\), \(\sum_n a_n=\infty\), and \(\sum_n a_n^2<\infty\)
\((\xi_{n+1})\) is martingale-difference noise with uniformly bounded conditional second moments
\((x_n)\) is almost surely bounded
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_n\to-b\) almost surely rather than \(x_n\to0\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The limiting-bias phenomenon fits the leaf, but the almost-sure convergence theorem is uncited. Positivity of the gain sequence should also be stated explicitly rather than inferred from terminology.

children.title: Constraint-Induced Dynamical Artifacts
children.top_down_role: Unintended limiting behavior induced by constraints.

children.title: Boundary Trapping
children.top_down_role: Persistent attraction to constraint boundaries caused by noisy or biased motion.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Trapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absorption at a constraint boundary under projected updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[0,\infty)\) and \(x_{n+1}=\Pi_C(x_n-a_n\widehat h_{n+1})\). If \(x_n=0\) and \(\widehat h_{n+1}\geq0\), then \(x_{n+1}=0\). Consequently, if \(x_N=0\) and \(\widehat h_{n+1}\geq0\) for every \(n\geq N\), then \(x_n=0\) for all \(n\geq N\). Projection therefore makes the boundary absorbing whenever the estimated update direction persistently points outside the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once a projected scalar recursion reaches zero, persistently outward estimated steps keep every subsequent iterate trapped at that boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(x_N=0\) and \(\widehat h_{n+1}\geq0\) for all \(n\geq N\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_n=0\) for all \(n\geq N\)

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the feasible set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar projection argument is correct and the failure-boundary kind fits, but no source or locator supports the boundary-trapping claim.

children.title: Projection-Induced Fixed Points
children.top_down_role: Spurious limiting states introduced by the projection geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Induced Fixed Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point characterization for a projected deterministic update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(a>0\), and define \(T(x)=\Pi_C(x-a h(x))\). For \(x\in C\),
\[T(x)=x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad-h(x)\in N_C(x),\]
where \(N_C(x)=\{v:\langle v,y-x\rangle\leq0\ \text{for all }y\in C\}\). Thus projection can create fixed points at boundary locations where \(h(x)\neq0\), because the outward component of the unprojected step lies in the normal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected update is fixed exactly when the negative update field lies in the constraint set’s normal cone.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex
\(x\in C\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi_C(x-a h(x))=x\Longleftrightarrow-h(x)\in N_C(x)\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-point equivalence uses the stated normal-cone convention correctly and fits the leaf, but this nontrivial projection characterization has no cited source.

children.title: Constraint-Face Cycling
children.top_down_role: Repeated motion among active faces or boundary regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Face Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A projected recursion cycling perpetually among boundary faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=[-1,1]^2\), let \(R(u,v)=(-v,u)\), and set \(T(x)=\Pi_C(Rx)\). Starting from \(x_0=(1,1)\), projection is inactive and
\[x_0=(1,1),\quad x_1=(-1,1),\quad x_2=(-1,-1),\quad x_3=(1,-1),\quad x_4=x_0.\]
Hence \(x_{n+1}=T(x_n)\) has a nonconvergent period-four orbit visiting four constraint faces. Equivalently, it is the projected update \(T(x)=\Pi_C(x-h(x))\) with \(h(x)=x-Rx\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rotation on a square produces a projected period-four orbit through its corners, so the constrained iterates never converge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{n+4}=x_n\) and \(x_{n+1}\neq x_n\) for all \(n\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The period-four orbit is correctly computed and the counterexample kind fits Constraint-Face Cycling, but the record lacks source support.

children.title: Nonstationary Tracking Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Mismatch between adaptation speed and changing simulation response.

children.title: Adaptation-Lag Failure
children.top_down_role: Tracking error caused by adaptation that is too slow for response changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptation-Lag Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent tracking error when target drift outpaces a constant-gain recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the target drift as \(\theta_{n+1}=\theta_n+v\) with \(v\neq0\), and let \(x_{n+1}=x_n+a(\theta_n-x_n)\) for \(a\in(0,1)\). Writing \(e_n=x_n-\theta_n\) gives \(e_{n+1}=(1-a)e_n-v\), hence
\[e_n\longrightarrow-\frac{v}{a}.\]
Therefore the recursion remains asymptotically separated from the moving target by \(|v|/a\); exact tracking fails for every nonzero drift speed at fixed gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With constant gain and linearly drifting target, the tracking error converges to a nonzero lag equal to minus drift divided by gain.
assumptions_latex: \(\theta_{n+1}=\theta_n+v\) with \(v\neq0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_n-\theta_n\to-v/a\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tracking-error recursion and limit are correct and match Adaptation-Lag Failure, but the failure-boundary claim has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Drifting-Response Regimes
children.top_down_role: Gradual evolution of simulator response during optimization.

assumptions_latex: The time-varying mean response is \(f_t:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\), with minimizer \(x_t^*\).
The recursion is \(x_{t+1}=x_t-a_t(\nabla f_t(x_t)+\varepsilon_{t+1})\), where \(\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_{t+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_t]=0\).
Each \(f_t\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex and has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(a_t\to0\) while \(\limsup_{t\to\infty}\|x_{t+1}^*-x_t^*\|/a_t>0\), then the stationary-convergence conclusion \(\|x_t-x_t^*\|\to0\) is not generally guaranteed. In particular, for \(d=1\), \(f_t(x)=\tfrac12(x-vt)^2\), \(v\ne0\), and noiseless constant-gain recursion with \(0<a<1\), the tracking error converges to \(-v/a\), not zero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth strongly convex objectives whose minimizers drift continually.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.1 Adaptive Noise Cancellation and Disturbance Rejection p. 77
source_refs.source_title: Stochastic Approximation and Recursive Algorithms and Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x_{t+1}=x_t-a_t(\nabla f_t(x_t)+\varepsilon_{t+1})\). Vanishing gains suppress noise but also reduce tracking bandwidth. A necessary scale separation for asymptotically negligible lag is that the optimizer displacement be small relative to the effective correction, namely \(\|x_{t+1}^*-x_t^*\|=o(a_t)\) under uniformly bounded local curvature. When this separation fails, tracking error need not vanish. The scalar quadratic family \(f_t(x)=\tfrac12(x-vt)^2\) makes the boundary explicit: with \(\varepsilon_t=0\) and constant \(a\in(0,1)\), the error \(e_t=x_t-vt\) satisfies \(e_{t+1}=(1-a)e_t-v\), hence \(e_t\to-v/a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic-approximation recursion can track a drifting optimum only when its correction scale dominates optimizer motion; otherwise persistent lag remains, even without observation noise.
knowledge_statements.title: Drifting-Response Regimes

children.title: Abrupt Regime Shifts
children.top_down_role: Sudden response changes that invalidate accumulated search information.

assumptions_latex: The objective equals \(f^-\) before a change time \(\tau\) and \(f^+\) afterward, with respective minimizers \(x^-\) and \(x^+\), where \(x^-\ne x^+\).
For the family of trajectories indexed by \(\tau\), the pre-change tracking error satisfies \(\|x_\tau-x^-\|\to0\) as \(\tau\to\infty\).
The noiseless recursion is \(x_{t+1}=x_t-a_t\nabla f_t(x_t)\), where \(a_t>0\) and \(a_t\to0\).
For every fixed integer \(m\ge1\), there is a finite constant \(G_m\) such that \(\|\nabla f^+(x_{\tau+j})\|\le G_m\) for \(j=0,\ldots,m-1\) and all sufficiently large \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every fixed integer \(m\ge1\), \(\|x_{\tau+m}-x^-\|\to0\) as \(\tau\to\infty\). Hence \(\|x_{\tau+m}-x^+\|\to\|x^--x^+\|>0\), so the recursion cannot uniformly reacquire the post-change minimizer within a fixed number of iterations after arbitrarily late changes.

notation.meaning: uniform post-change gradient bound over a fixed horizon of length m

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Late, nonvanishing optimizer jumps under a noiseless recursion with vanishing gains and asymptotically negligible pre-change tracking error.

children.top_down_role: Local model-based search with adaptive regions and simulation precision.

children.title: Stochastic Response-Surface Trust Regions
children.top_down_role: Local polynomial models coupled to region adaptation.

assumptions_latex: The simulator returns \(Y(x,\xi)\) with \(\mathbb{E}[Y(x,\xi)]=f(x)\) for \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\).
A local polynomial model can be fitted from sampled design sites in each trust region.
Estimated objective reductions are available at trial and incumbent points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the final incumbent \(x_k\); accepted steps have sufficiently large estimated actual-to-predicted reduction, while rejected steps shrink the region.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free local polynomial trust-region method for noisy simulation responses.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in X\), \(\Delta_0>0\), and thresholds \(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\), iteration \(k\) samples design sites in \(X\cap B(x_k,\Delta_k)\) and fits a local polynomial \(m_k\). Compute \(s_k\in\arg\min\{m_k(x_k+s):x_k+s\in X,\ \|s\|\le\Delta_k\}\). From simulation estimates \(\widehat f_k\), form \(\widehat\rho_k=[\widehat f_k(x_k)-\widehat f_k(x_k+s_k)]/[m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)]\). Accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) when \(\widehat\rho_k\ge\eta_1\), otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Shrink, retain, or enlarge \(\Delta_k\) according as \(\widehat\rho_k<\eta_1\), \(\eta_1\le\widehat\rho_k<\eta_2\), or \(\widehat\rho_k\ge\eta_2\), and stop under a prescribed budget or stationarity rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit a local polynomial from simulations, minimize it within a trust region, and adapt the region using estimated actual versus predicted improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Response-Surface Trust Regions

children.title: Adaptive-Sampling Trust Regions
children.top_down_role: Region decisions coupled to dynamically controlled estimator precision.

assumptions_latex: The simulator supplies estimators of objective values whose precision increases with replication count.
A trust-region model \(m_k\), center \(x_k\), and radius \(\Delta_k>0\) are maintained.
Sampling can continue until a prescribed confidence or error tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each acceptance decision is made only after estimator uncertainty is small relative to the predicted reduction or the sampling budget is exhausted; the algorithm returns the final incumbent.

notation.meaning: half-width or error bound for reduction estimation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region acceptance with sampling precision tied to predicted improvement.

source_refs.locator: 3. Simulation-Based Optimization: An Overview p. 29
source_refs.source_title: Simulation-Based Optimization: Parametric Optimization Techniques and Reinforcement Learning

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), compute a trial step \(s_k\) with predicted reduction \(p_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)>0\). Draw paired or independent replications at \(x_k\) and \(x_k+s_k\) until a valid error bound \(h_k\) for the estimated reduction \(\widehat d_k\) satisfies \(h_k\le\kappa p_k\), for fixed \(\kappa>0\), or a sampling cap is reached. Set \(\widehat\rho_k=\widehat d_k/p_k\), accept the trial point when \(\widehat\rho_k\ge\eta\), and update \(\Delta_k\) by the trust-region acceptance rule. If the precision condition fails at the cap, declare the comparison unresolved and do not enlarge the region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase simulation effort until uncertainty is small relative to predicted improvement, then use the resulting comparison to accept the step and adapt the region.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Sampling Trust Regions

children.title: Trust-Region Reliability Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Model-accuracy, growing-sample, and noise-dominance regimes.

children.title: Probabilistically Accurate Model Regime
children.top_down_role: Convergence supported by recurring local-model reliability.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), the random model \(M_k\) is measurable after new simulation data are collected.
The true objective \(f\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of every trust region.
The model gradient and function errors are assessed on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the conditional probability bound holds uniformly in \(k\), accurate iterations recur with probability controlled away from zero; convergence theorems additionally require suitable acceptance, radius-update, and estimator conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistically fully linear models for smooth trust-region optimization.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Response surface methodology p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constants \(\kappa_f,\kappa_g>0\), call \(M_k\) accurate on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\) when, simultaneously for every \(y\in B(x_k,\Delta_k)\), \(|f(y)-M_k(y)|\le\kappa_f\Delta_k^2\) and \(\|\nabla f(y)-\nabla M_k(y)\|\le\kappa_g\Delta_k\). The probabilistically accurate model regime holds when there exists \(p>1/2\) such that \(\mathbb{P}(M_k\text{ is accurate}\mid\mathcal{F}_{k-1})\ge p\) almost surely for every \(k\). This condition expresses recurring scale-correct local reliability rather than requiring every random model to be accurate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model is probabilistically accurate when, conditionally on the past, it satisfies trust-region-scaled function and gradient error bounds with probability uniformly above one half.
knowledge_statements.title: Probabilistically Accurate Model Regime

children.title: Growing-Sample Regime
children.top_down_role: Convergence supported by increasing local simulation precision.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), sample means are formed from independent replications with finite variances uniformly bounded near the iterates.
The trust-region radius is \(\Delta_k>0\), and model fitting uses finitely many local design sites.
Replication counts \(N_k\) may depend on the observed history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed growth conditions force sampling errors to vanish at the scales required for function-value and gradient-model accuracy, supporting increasingly reliable trust-region decisions.

notation.meaning: minimum replication count per local estimate at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Increasing replication counts relative to shrinking trust-region scales.

source_refs.locator: 3. Simulation-Based Optimization: An Overview p. 29
source_refs.source_title: Simulation-Based Optimization: Parametric Optimization Techniques and Reinforcement Learning

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A growing-sample trust-region regime requires \(N_k\to\infty\) along iterations where additional precision is needed. For sample-mean function estimates, a scale-compatible sufficient requirement is \(s_k/\sqrt{N_k}=o(\Delta_k^2)\) in probability, where \(s_k^2\) estimates the simulation variance. Equivalently under uniformly bounded variances, one may impose \(N_k\Delta_k^4\to\infty\). If local gradient coefficients are obtained by differencing function estimates across distances of order \(\Delta_k\), the same condition makes the induced gradient error \(o(\Delta_k)\). Sampling rules may enforce these relations adaptively through confidence bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replication counts grow fast enough that simulation error becomes negligible relative to the trust-region function and gradient accuracy scales.
knowledge_statements.title: Growing-Sample Regime

The mathematical formulation depends on variance estimation, design geometry, and model-fitting assumptions that require a trust-region sampling source.

children.title: Noise-Dominated Region Failure
children.top_down_role: Region collapse or false acceptance caused by unresolved simulation error.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), a trial step has true reduction \(d_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)\) and predicted reduction \(p_k>0\).
The estimated reduction is \(\widehat d_k=d_k+e_k\), and a valid deterministic or eventwise error bound \(b_k\ge|e_k|\) is available.
Acceptance uses \(\widehat d_k/p_k\ge\eta\), where \(\eta\in(0,1)\).
After a rejection, the radius update satisfies \(\Delta_{k+1}\le\gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}\Delta_k\) for some \(\gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance is certified when \(\widehat d_k-b_k\ge\eta p_k\), and rejection is certified when \(\widehat d_k+b_k<\eta p_k\). If \(b_k\ge|d_k-\eta p_k|\), the error bound alone does not certify which side of the true acceptance threshold contains \(d_k\). Errors crossing that margin can reverse the decision, and an indefinitely repeated sequence of false rejections contracts \(\Delta_k\) geometrically without by itself establishing stationarity.

notation.meaning: reduction-estimation error and its valid bound
trust-region radius and rejection contraction factor

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance decisions whose reduction signal is unresolved at the trust-region decision scale.

source_refs.locator: 3. Simulation-Based Optimization: An Overview p. 29
source_refs.source_title: Simulation-Based Optimization: Parametric Optimization Techniques and Reinforcement Learning

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat d_k=d_k+e_k\), where \(d_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)\), and suppose \(b_k\ge|e_k|\). Under the rule that accepts when \(\widehat d_k/p_k\ge\eta\), acceptance is certified if \(\widehat d_k-b_k\ge\eta p_k\), while rejection is certified if \(\widehat d_k+b_k<\eta p_k\). If \(b_k\ge|d_k-\eta p_k|\), the available error bound does not prevent the estimate from crossing the true decision margin. In particular, \(d_k\ge\eta p_k\) with \(e_k<-(d_k-\eta p_k)\) causes false rejection, whereas \(d_k<\eta p_k\) with \(e_k\ge\eta p_k-d_k\) causes false acceptance. If every rejection satisfies \(\Delta_{k+1}\le\gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}\Delta_k\) with \(0<\gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}<1\), indefinitely repeated false rejections force \(\Delta_k\to0\) without themselves establishing stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the reduction-error bound is at least as large as the acceptance margin, the comparison is uncertified and realized noise can reverse the trust-region decision; repeated false rejections can then contract the radius without proving stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Dominated Region Failure

children.top_down_role: Optimization performed on fixed simulated random-input paths.

children.title: Common-Sample-Path Optimization
children.top_down_role: Optimization using a shared fixed collection of random inputs.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\).
The random input \(\xi\) has distribution \(P\), and \(F(x,\xi)\) is measurable with finite expectation for every \(x\in X\).
One fixed sample \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) is reused for all candidate decisions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conditional on the fixed sample, the problem is deterministic; the shared paths induce dependence among \(\widehat f_N(x)\) across alternatives while preserving their pointwise sample-average form.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed common random inputs reused across the entire decision space.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic optimization procedures and their stochastic counterparts p. 22

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\mathbb{E}[F(x,\xi)]\), draw \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) once and define the common-sample-path objective \(\widehat f_N(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N F(x,\xi_i)\) for every \(x\in X\). Common-sample-path optimization solves \(\widehat x_N\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\widehat f_N(x)\) while keeping exactly the same realized inputs for every objective comparison and every optimization iteration. Thus randomness is frozen before optimization; it is not resampled when \(x\) changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Draw one set of random inputs, reuse it for every candidate decision, and optimize the resulting deterministic sample-path objective.

children.title: Retrospective Approximation
children.top_down_role: A sequence of increasingly accurate sample-path optimization problems.

assumptions_latex: The target is \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\), where \(f(x)=\mathbb{E}[F(x,\xi)]\).
Stage sample sizes satisfy \(N_1<N_2<\cdots\) and \(N_k\to\infty\).
Each stage admits a specified optimization tolerance \(\epsilon_k\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs the stage incumbents \((x_k)\) or its last member; under separate consistency and vanishing-tolerance hypotheses, accumulation points may inherit optimality for the expected-value problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential sample-path problems with growing samples and controlled solution accuracy.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic optimization procedures and their stochastic counterparts p. 22

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose increasing sample sizes \(N_k\), stage tolerances \(\epsilon_k\), and an initial point \(x_0\in X\). At stage \(k\), construct \(\widehat f_{N_k}(x)=N_k^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{N_k}F(x,\xi_i)\), optionally retaining earlier observations, and initialize the deterministic solver from \(x_{k-1}\). Compute \(x_k\in X\) satisfying \(\widehat f_{N_k}(x_k)\le\inf_{x\in X}\widehat f_{N_k}(x)+\epsilon_k\). Increase \(N_k\), tighten \(\epsilon_k\) according to the prescribed schedule, and stop when the simulation budget or a statistical and optimization stopping criterion is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a sequence of increasingly large sample-path problems, warm-starting each stage and coordinating optimization tolerance with improving sampling accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Retrospective Approximation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonterminating retrospective approximation algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retrospective approximation repeatedly solves increasingly large sample-path problems with vanishing optimization tolerances and forms weighted averages of the resulting solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose sample sizes \(m_k\to\infty\), error tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), and weights \(\{w_{kj}:1\leq j\leq k\}\) for each iteration. Initialize \(k=1\). At iteration \(k\), generate a sample-path problem of size \(m_k\), use \(\bar X_{k-1}\) as a warm start, and compute a retrospective solution \(X_k\) to tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\). Set \[\bar X_k=\sum_{j=1}^k w_{kj}X_j,\] replace \(k\) by \(k+1\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each retrospective iteration, solve a larger sample-path problem to a smaller tolerance using the preceding averaged solution as a warm start, form a weighted sum of all retrospective solutions obtained so far, and continue without a termination step.

\varepsilon_k\to0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-sure consistency of retrospective solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure convergence of retrospective-solution objective error and distance to the true global-minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that \(\Theta\) is compact; the global-minimizer set \(\pi^*\) of \(f\) is nonempty; \(f\) is continuous on \(\Theta\); \(f_n\to f\) uniformly almost surely; and the global-minimizer sets \(\Pi_n^*\) of \(f_n\) are nonempty for all sufficiently large \(n\) almost surely. In retrospective approximation, suppose \(m_k\to\infty\), \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), and, for every fixed positive integer \(s\), \[\sum_{j=1}^s w_{ij}\to0\quad\text{as }i\to\infty.\] Whenever \(\Pi_{m_k}^*\neq\varnothing\), let \(X_k\) satisfy \[\left|f_{m_k}(X_k)-v_{m_k}^*\right|\leq\varepsilon_k,\qquad v_{m_k}^*:=\inf_{x\in\Theta}f_{m_k}(x).\] Then, almost surely, \[f(X_k)-v^*\to0\quad\text{and}\quad d(X_k,\pi^*)\to0,\] where the distance is assigned the value \(\infty\) if \(\Pi_{m_k}^*=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the feasible set is compact, the true objective is continuous, the sample objectives converge uniformly almost surely, sample minimizers eventually exist, sample sizes diverge, solution tolerances vanish, and every fixed initial block of weights has vanishing total weight, then retrospective solutions converge almost surely in true objective value and in distance to the true global-minimizer set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sample Average Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-sample empirical objective, deterministic optimization problem, and optimizer estimator in simulation optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given fixed samples \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\), each distributed as \(\xi\), define \(f_n(x)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^nY(x,\xi_i)\) and solve \(\min_{x\in\Theta}f_n(x)\). Conditional on the fixed sample, \(f_n\) is deterministic. An optimizer \(X_n^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\Theta}f_n(x)\) is used as an estimator of an optimal solution of the expectation problem. Unless otherwise stated, the sample is i.i.d.; independence may be relaxed deliberately in variance-reduction or randomized quasi-Monte Carlo schemes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SAA replaces the expectation objective with the average response over a fixed sample. Conditional on that sample, the problem is deterministic, and an optimizer is used to estimate a solution of the original expectation problem. Sampling is ordinarily i.i.d., although some variance-reduction and randomized quasi-Monte Carlo schemes deliberately introduce dependence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sample-average approximation of a newsvendor expectation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equally weighted finite-sample approximation of expected newsvendor profit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\widehat D\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(\mu)\), then \[F(x\mid\mu)=\sum_{d=0}^{\infty}\frac{\mu^d e^{-\mu}}{d!}\bigl(p\min\{x,d\}-cx\bigr).\] Given a finite nonempty sample indexed by \(\widehat\Omega\), with all sampled outcomes assigned equal weight, \[\bar F(x)=\frac{1}{|\widehat\Omega|}\sum_{\omega\in\widehat\Omega}\bigl(p\min\{x,\widehat D(\omega)\}-cx\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For Poisson demand, expected newsvendor profit is a probability-weighted infinite sum. A finite sample treated as equally weighted approximates this expectation by the arithmetic mean of the sampled profits.

children.title: Single-Sample SAA
children.top_down_role: Optimization of one sampled approximation.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\).
The loss \(F(x,\xi)\) is measurable and integrable for every \(x\in X\).
A single independent sample \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any selected \(\widehat x_N\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\widehat f_N(x)\) is a single-sample SAA solution, and \(\widehat v_N\) is its in-sample optimal value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One independently sampled empirical approximation of an expected-value problem.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Stochastic optimization problems p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given one independent sample \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\), define \(\widehat f_N(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N F(x,\xi_i)\) for \(x\in X\). A single-sample sample-average approximation replaces \(\min_{x\in X}\mathbb{E}[F(x,\xi)]\) by the deterministic empirical problem \(\widehat v_N=\min_{x\in X}\widehat f_N(x)\). Any measurable selection \(\widehat x_N\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\widehat f_N(x)\) is its solution. All optimization decisions for this problem use that one realized sample; additional independent samples are reserved for validation rather than redefining this SAA instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-sample SAA replaces an expected objective by one empirical average and optimizes that fixed sampled problem.

Each replicated SAA problem has a computable optimizer and optimal value.

Summarize sampling variability using the empirical distribution of \(\widehat v_N^{(1)},\ldots,\widehat v_N^{(R)}\). Evaluate each distinct candidate \(\widehat x_N^{(r)}\) on an independent validation sample, select the candidate with the smallest prescribed validated estimate or confidence bound, and report both its validation uncertainty and the replicated-value summary.

children.title: Adaptive-Sample-Size SAA
children.top_down_role: Sample sizes coordinated with optimization progress.

assumptions_latex: The objective is \(f(x)=\mathbb{E}[F(x,\xi)]\) over \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\).
A nested or independently expandable sample stream is available.
At each stage, computable statistical and optimization error indicators are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns the last incumbent; sample size increases only when estimated sampling error is too large relative to the current optimization requirement or stopping tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SAA sample growth triggered by estimated statistical versus optimization error.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic optimization procedures and their stochastic counterparts p. 22

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(N_0\), \(x_0\in X\), and tolerances \(\tau_k>0\). At stage \(k\), form \(\widehat f_{N_k}(x)=N_k^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{N_k}F(x,\xi_i)\) and approximately minimize it from \(x_{k-1}\) until \(E_k^{\mathrm{opt}}\le c_{\mathrm{opt}}\tau_k\). Estimate sampling error \(E_k^{\mathrm{samp}}\) using independent validation, resampling, or a valid variance bound. If \(E_k^{\mathrm{samp}}>c_{\mathrm{samp}}\tau_k\), choose \(N_{k+1}>N_k\), augment or redraw the sample, and continue; otherwise stop when \(\tau_k\) meets the requested accuracy, or tighten \(\tau_k\) and repeat. Output the final incumbent and its error indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the SAA sample only when estimated statistical error is too large for the current optimization accuracy, then continue from the current solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact recovery of a sharp SAA optimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure eventual identification and exponential-probability recovery of a sharp true optimizer by sample average approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the true problem is convex, assumption (M1) holds, and \(x^*\in X\) is a sharp optimal solution. Then, with probability one, \(\widehat S_N=\{x^*\}\) for all sufficiently large \(N\). If assumption (M4) also holds, then there exist constants \(C>0\) and \(\beta>0\) such that \[1-\Pr\!\left(\widehat S_N=\{x^*\}\right)\leq Ce^{-N\beta}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex problem satisfying (M1), a sharp true optimizer is eventually the unique SAA optimizer almost surely. Under (M4), the probability of failure to identify it uniquely decreases exponentially with the sample size.
assumptions_latex: \text{The true problem is convex and satisfies (M1).}
x^*\in X\text{ is a sharp optimal solution.}
\text{The exponential bound additionally requires (M4).}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr\!\left(\exists N_0\;\forall N\geq N_0:\widehat S_N=\{x^*\}\right)=1,\qquad \exists C,\beta>0:\ 1-\Pr\!\left(\widehat S_N=\{x^*\}\right)\leq Ce^{-N\beta}\ \text{ under (M4)}.

children.title: SAA Optimal-Value Consistency
children.top_down_role: Convergence behavior of sampled optimal values relative to target values.

knowledge_statements.title: SAA Optimal-Value Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure optimal-value consistency under uniform convergence on a compact feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be nonempty and compact, let \(F:X\times\Xi\to\mathbb{R}\) be measurable in its second argument, and define \(f(x)=\mathbb{E}[F(x,\xi)]\) and \(f_N(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N F(x,\xi_i)\), where \(\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots\) are iid copies of \(\xi\). If \(f\) is finite and continuous on \(X\) and \(\sup_{x\in X}|f_N(x)-f(x)|\to0\) almost surely, then, with \(v=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) and \(v_N=\inf_{x\in X}f_N(x)\), one has \[|v_N-v|\leq \sup_{x\in X}|f_N(x)-f(x)|\to0\quad\text{almost surely}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform almost-sure convergence of the SAA objectives implies almost-sure convergence of their infimal values to the attained population optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\) is compact and \(f\) is finite and continuous on \(X\).
\(\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots\) are iid copies of \(\xi\).
\(\sup_{x\in X}|f_N(x)-f(x)|\to0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_N\to v\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: population minimum and SAA infimal value

children.title: SAA Solution-Set Convergence
children.top_down_role: Setwise convergence behavior of sampled optimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: SAA Solution-Set Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer convergence of exact or asymptotically optimal SAA solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the setting of SAA optimal-value consistency, let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\), and choose \(x_N\in X\) satisfying \(f_N(x_N)\leq v_N+\varepsilon_N\), where \(\varepsilon_N\to0\) almost surely. If \(\sup_{x\in X}|f_N(x)-f(x)|\to0\) almost surely, then \[\operatorname{dist}(x_N,S)\to0\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Equivalently, every accumulation point of \((x_N)\) belongs to \(S\). Consequently, the outer deviation of the exact SAA solution set \(S_N=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f_N(x)\) from \(S\) converges to zero whenever each \(S_N\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every limit point of asymptotically optimal SAA solutions is truly optimal; exact SAA solution sets therefore converge to the true set in outer deviation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and compact, and \(f\) is continuous.
\(\sup_{x\in X}|f_N(x)-f(x)|\to0\) almost surely.
\(f_N(x_N)\leq v_N+\varepsilon_N\) with \(\varepsilon_N\to0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x_N,S)\to0\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: distance from a point to the set S

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The outer solution-set convergence claim is mathematically consistent with compactness, continuity, uniform convergence, and nonempty SAA argmin sets, but no inspectable source is cited.

children.title: SAA Optimizer Selection Stability
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of selected sampled optimizers across increasing or repeated samples.

knowledge_statements.title: SAA Optimizer Selection Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stable selection when the population optimizer is unique and uniformly separated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous with unique minimizer \(x^\star\), and suppose \(\sup_{x\in X}|f_N(x)-f(x)|\to0\) almost surely. For every open neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^\star\) such that \(X\setminus U\neq\varnothing\), define \(\gamma_U=\inf_{x\in X\setminus U}f(x)-f(x^\star)\). Then \(\gamma_U>0\), and whenever \(2\sup_{x\in X}|f_N(x)-f(x)|<\gamma_U\), every exact SAA minimizer lies in \(U\). If each SAA argmin is nonempty, every measurable selection \(x_N\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f_N(x)\) satisfies \(x_N\to x^\star\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unique population optimizer and uniform objective convergence force every exact SAA optimizer selection to converge almost surely to that optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and \(f\) is continuous with unique minimizer \(x^\star\).
\(\sup_{x\in X}|f_N(x)-f(x)|\to0\) almost surely.
Each SAA argmin is nonempty and the selected optimizer is measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_N\to x^\star\) almost surely for every measurable exact-optimizer selection.

notation.meaning: population objective separation outside the neighborhood U

children.title: SAA Optimality-Gap Bounds
children.top_down_role: Statistical bounds for candidate solution quality.

knowledge_statements.title: SAA Optimality-Gap Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic population-gap certificate derived from uniform SAA error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\neq\varnothing\), let \(f,f_N:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and suppose that for some \(\eta\geq0\), \(\sup_{x\in X}|f_N(x)-f(x)|\leq\eta\). For any \(\widehat{x}\in X\), define \(v=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\) and \(v_N=\inf_{x\in X}f_N(x)\). Then \[0\leq f(\widehat{x})-v\leq f_N(\widehat{x})-v_N+2\eta.\] In particular, if \(f_N(\widehat{x})\leq v_N+\varepsilon\) for some \(\varepsilon\geq0\), then \(f(\widehat{x})-v\leq\varepsilon+2\eta\). If the uniform-error event has probability at least \(1-\delta\) for \(\delta\in(0,1)\), the certificate holds with at least that probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empirical optimality gap plus twice a uniform objective-error bound certifies the candidate's population optimality gap.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\), \(\widehat{x}\in X\), and \(f,f_N:X\to\mathbb{R}\).
\(\eta\geq0\) and \(\sup_{x\in X}|f_N(x)-f(x)|\leq\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\widehat{x})-v\leq f_N(\widehat{x})-v_N+2\eta\).

children.title: SAA Accuracy-Cost Complexity Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Simulation and optimization effort needed for target accuracy.

children.title: SAA Sample Complexity
children.top_down_role: Sampling effort associated with prescribed reliability or accuracy targets.

knowledge_statements.title: SAA Sample Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-class high-probability sample bound for an exact SAA optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) contain \(M<\infty\) decisions. For every \(x\in X\), suppose \(F(x,\xi)\) lies almost surely in an interval of length at most \(B\), and define \(f(x)=\mathbb{E}[F(x,\xi)]\). From common iid samples \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\), define \(f_N(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N F(x,\xi_i)\), and let \(\widehat{x}_N\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f_N(x)\). For \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(\delta\in(0,1)\), \[N\geq \frac{2B^2}{\varepsilon^2}\log\!\left(\frac{2M}{\delta}\right)\] suffices for \(f(\widehat{x}_N)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\leq\varepsilon\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite decision class with bounded losses, order epsilon to the minus two times log(M/delta) samples suffice for epsilon-optimality with confidence 1-delta.
assumptions_latex: \(|X|=M<\infty\).
For every \(x\in X\), \(F(x,\xi)\) lies almost surely in an interval of length at most \(B\).
\(\xi_1,[0m\ldots,\xi_N\) are iid, \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(\delta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{P}\{f(\widehat{x}_N)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\leq\varepsilon\}\geq1-\delta\) under the displayed sample bound.

notation.meaning: uniform upper bound on loss-range length

children.title: SAA Optimization-Work Complexity
children.top_down_role: Computational effort required to solve sampled optimization problems.

knowledge_statements.title: SAA Optimization-Work Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simulation and comparison work for exhaustive finite-class SAA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) contain \(M<\infty\) decisions, let \(N\geq1\), compute \(f_N(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N F(x,\xi_i)\) for every \(x\in X\), and return a decision attaining \(\min_{x\in X}f_N(x)\). If each evaluation of \(F(x,\xi_i)\) has unit simulation cost, exhaustive SAA uses exactly \(MN\) loss evaluations, \(M(N-1)\) additions for the sample totals, and \(M-1\) comparisons to find a minimum. Under the bounded-loss assumptions of the finite-class sample bound, choosing \[N=\left\lceil\frac{2B^2}{\varepsilon^2}\log\!\left(\frac{2M}{\delta}\right)\right\rceil\] gives \(MN=O\!\left(MB^2\varepsilon^{-2}\log(M/\delta)\right)\) loss evaluations and is sufficient for an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal population decision with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive finite-class SAA uses MN loss evaluations, giving work of order MB squared times epsilon to the minus two times log(M/delta) under the stated accuracy guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(|X|=M<\infty\), \(N\geq1\), and exhaustive enumeration is used.
Each loss evaluation has unit simulation cost.
Losses satisfy the bounded-range assumptions of the finite-class sample-complexity result, with \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(\delta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(MN=O\!\left(MB^2\varepsilon^{-2}\log(M/\delta)\right)\) loss evaluations suffice.

notation.meaning: total number of simulated loss evaluations

children.title: SAA Accuracy-Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Joint effects of sample size, solve effort, and target accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: SAA Accuracy-Cost Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-class confidence bound expressed under a fixed simulation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) contain \(M<\infty\) decisions, define \(f(x)=\mathbb{E}[F(x,\xi)]\), and suppose every \(F(x,\xi)\) lies almost surely in an interval of length at most \(B\). Given a total loss-evaluation budget \(T\geq M\), use \(N=\lfloor T/M\rfloor\) common iid observations to form \(f_N(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N F(x,\xi_i)\) for every \(x\in X\), and let \(\widehat{x}_N\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f_N(x)\). For every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), with probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[f(\widehat{x}_N)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\leq B\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2M/\delta)}{N}}.\] Thus, for fixed \(M\), the certified error is of order \(T^{-1/2}\); increasing \(M\) reduces the sample allocation per decision and increases the logarithmic multiple-comparison factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal budget allocation yields an optimality-gap bound proportional to the square root of M log(M/delta) divided by T, exposing the tradeoff between search breadth and estimation accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(|X|=M<\infty\), \(T\geq M\), and \(\delta\in(0,1)\).
\(N=\lfloor T/M\rfloor\) common iid observations are used for every decision.
Every loss has almost-sure range length at most \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\widehat{x}_N)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\leq B\sqrt{2\log(2M/\delta)/\lfloor T/M\rfloor}\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: common sample size used for each decision

children.title: SAA Generalization Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Unstable decisions caused by undersized or unrepresentative samples.

children.title: SAA Sample-Induced Overfitting
children.top_down_role: Excessive adaptation of decisions to a particular sampled problem.

knowledge_statements.title: SAA Sample-Induced Overfitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential decision multiplicity creates persistent empirical optimism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each sample size \(N\), let \(X_N=\{1,\ldots,2^N\}\), and let \(F(x,\xi_i)\) be mutually independent Bernoulli random variables with mean \(1/2\) across both \(x\) and \(i\). Every decision has population value \(f(x)=1/2\). Nevertheless, the probability that at least one decision has zero loss on all \(N\) observations is \[1-(1-2^{-N})^{2^N}\geq 1-e^{-1}.\] On this event, the SAA optimum is \(v_N=0\), although every selected empirical optimizer has population value \(1/2\). Hence the in-sample optimum understates its selected decision's true value by \(1/2\) with nonvanishing probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exponentially many independent candidates, SAA finds a perfectly fitting candidate with constant probability even though every candidate’s true loss is one-half.
assumptions_latex: The variables \(F(x,\xi_i)\) are mutually independent Bernoulli variables of mean \(1/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{P}\{v_N=0\}\geq1-e^{-1}\) while \(f(x)=1/2\) for every \(x\in X_N\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constructed exponential-class overfitting example and probability calculation are coherent, and counterexample is the correct terminal kind, but no source or registered independent verification is supplied.

children.title: SAA Optimizer Selection Instability
children.top_down_role: Large decision changes across comparable sampled problems.

knowledge_statements.title: SAA Optimizer Selection Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonunique population optima prevent convergence to a fixed selected optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{a,b\}\), and for each observation let \(F(a,\xi_i)\) and \(F(b,\xi_i)\) be independent Bernoulli random variables with mean \(1/2\). Then \(a\) and \(b\) are both population optimizers. Select the smaller empirical-loss decision, breaking ties in favor of \(a\). Symmetry and the vanishing probability of equal sample sums give \[\mathbb{P}\{\widehat{x}_N=a\}\to\frac12,\qquad \mathbb{P}\{\widehat{x}_N=b\}\to\frac12.\] Thus the selected optimizer does not converge in probability to either fixed decision, even though its distance to the population solution set is always zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When two population optimizers tie, sampling noise can keep switching the selected SAA optimizer, despite perfect solution-set consistency.
assumptions_latex: Losses are independent Bernoulli variables of mean \(1/2\) across decisions and observations.
Empirical ties are resolved in favor of \(a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat{x}_N\) converges to neither \(a\) nor \(b\) in probability.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Bernoulli tie example correctly separates solution-set consistency from convergence to a fixed selected optimizer, but the constructed failure boundary lacks a source or registered independent verification.

children.title: SAA Out-of-Sample Degradation
children.top_down_role: Performance loss when sampled solutions are evaluated on independent simulation output.

knowledge_statements.title: SAA Out-of-Sample Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large candidate classes can produce a fixed positive out-of-sample gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(N\geq1\), let \(X_N=\{0,1,2,\ldots,2^N\}\). Set \(F(0,\xi_i)=1/4\) deterministically. For every \(x\in\{1,\ldots,2^N\}\), let the variables \(F(x,\xi_i)\) be mutually independent across \(x\) and \(i\), with Bernoulli distribution of mean \(1/2\). Decision \(0\) is the unique population minimizer. With probability \[1-(1-2^{-N})^{2^N}\geq1-e^{-1},\] at least one inferior decision has empirical average zero, so every exact empirical minimizer is inferior. On this event, its population value is \(1/2\), its population optimality gap is \(1/4\), and its in-sample value is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Searching exponentially many inferior candidates selects a zero-training-loss candidate with a fixed positive population gap with probability at least 1 minus e to the minus one.
assumptions_latex: \(F(0,\xi_i)=1/4\) deterministically.
For \(x\geq1\), the losses are mutually independent across decisions and observations and are Bernoulli with mean \(1/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{P}\{f(\widehat{x}_N)-f(0)=1/4\}\geq1-e^{-1}\) for every exact empirical minimizer \(\widehat{x}_N\).

children.title: Model-Reference Adaptive Search
children.top_down_role: Adaptive sampling-distribution search guided by strong simulated outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Reference Adaptive Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Idealized MRAS update using an elite reference distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a search space \(X\), objective \(H:X\to\mathbb{R}\) to maximize, parametric densities \(q_\theta\), sample size \(m\), and elite fraction \(\rho\in(0,1)\), initialize \(\theta_0\). At iteration \(k\), draw \(X_{k,1},\ldots,X_{k,m}\sim q_{\theta_k}\), evaluate \(H\), and let \(\gamma_k\) be their empirical \((1-\rho)\)-quantile. Form reference weights \(w_{k,j}=S(H(X_{k,j}))\mathbf{1}\{H(X_{k,j})\geq\gamma_k\}/q_{\theta_k}(X_{k,j})\), where \(S>0\) is nondecreasing. Update \[\theta_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\theta}\sum_{j=1}^m w_{k,j}\log q_\theta(X_{k,j}).\] Stop by a prescribed budget or parameter tolerance and return the best sampled point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MRAS repeatedly samples candidates, constructs an elite performance-weighted reference distribution, and fits the next parametric sampling law to that reference.
assumptions_latex: \(q_\theta(x)>0\) at every sampled point receiving positive reference weight.
The weighted maximum-likelihood update has an admissible solution.
\(S:\mathbb{R}\to(0,\infty)\) is nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta_{k+1}\) is a weighted maximum-likelihood projection of the elite reference distribution onto \(\{q_\theta\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Entropy Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elite-sample maximum-likelihood update for parametric global search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a minimization objective \(H:X\to\mathbb{R}\), parametric sampling densities \(q_\theta\), sample size \(m\), and elite fraction \(\rho\in(0,1)\), initialize \(\theta_0\). At iteration \(k\), independently draw \(X_{k,1},\ldots,X_{k,m}\sim q_{\theta_k}\), evaluate \(H(X_{k,j})\), and let \(\gamma_k\) be the empirical \(\rho\)-quantile. assumptions_latex: The family \(\{q_\theta\}\) supports sampling and maximum-likelihood fitting.
\(m\geq1\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\).
The elite set \(E_k\) is nonempty under the adopted quantile convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_{\theta_{k+1}}\) is the maximum-likelihood fit to the current elite sample.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cross-Entropy Optimization and Gaussian Elite-Sample Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposal-distribution adaptation by elite-sample fitting, including the multivariate-normal maximum-likelihood update; no convergence-to-global-optima guarantee is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The cross-entropy method maintains a proposal distribution in a parameterized family \(\{P_\theta\}\). At each iteration, it draws samples from the current proposal, selects the \(m_{\mathrm{elite}}\) samples having the best objective values, and fits the next proposal distribution to those elite samples. For a multivariate-normal proposal and elite samples \(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(m_{\mathrm{elite}})}\), maximum-likelihood fitting gives
\[\mu^{(k+1)}=\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{elite}}}\sum_{i=1}^{m_{\mathrm{elite}}}x^{(i)},\qquad \Sigma^{(k+1)}=\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{elite}}}\sum_{i=1}^{m_{\mathrm{elite}}}(x^{(i)}-\mu^{(k+1)})(x^{(i)}-\mu^{(k+1)})^\top.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cross-entropy method samples from a parameterized proposal distribution, retains the samples with the best objective values, and refits the proposal to those elite samples. For a multivariate normal proposal, maximum-likelihood fitting uses the elite-sample mean and the covariance with divisor equal to the elite-sample count. The stated aim of concentrating near global optima is not a convergence guarantee.
assumptions_latex: m_{\mathrm{elite}}\ge 1
x^{(i)}\in\mathbb R^d\quad(i=1,\ldots,m_{\mathrm{elite}})
P_\theta=\mathcal N(\mu,\Sigma)\text{ for the displayed analytic update}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu^{(k+1)}=\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{elite}}}\sum_{i=1}^{m_{\mathrm{elite}}}x^{(i)},\quad \Sigma^{(k+1)}=\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{elite}}}\sum_{i=1}^{m_{\mathrm{elite}}}(x^{(i)}-\mu^{(k+1)})(x^{(i)}-\mu^{(k+1)})^\top

children.title: Noisy Simulated Annealing

assumptions_latex: The state space \(S\) is finite, and a proposal kernel \(Q\) connects the states through an irreducible neighborhood graph.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(X_0\in S\). At iteration \(k\), propose \(Y_k\sim Q(X_k,\cdot)\), obtain simulation estimates at \(X_k\) and \(Y_k\), and set
\[
a_k=\min\left\{1,\frac{Q(Y_k,X_k)}{Q(X_k,Y_k)}\exp\left(-\frac{\widehat f_k(Y_k)-\widehat f_k(X_k)}{T_k}\right)\right\}.
\]
With an independent \(U_k\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\), take \(X_{k+1}=Y_k\) when \(U_k\leq a_k\), and otherwise take \(X_{k+1}=X_k\). Continue under a prescribed cooling and replication schedule; at termination, resample visited candidates as required and return the candidate with the smallest final estimated loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propose a neighboring state and accept it using a Metropolis probability computed from simulation-based loss estimates and the current temperature.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(\theta_0\in D\), gain sequence \((a_k)\), and temperature sequence \(T_k\downarrow0\). At iteration \(k\), generate a temperature-dependent perturbation and simulation output from which a direction estimate \(G_k\) is formed, then update
\[

Stop at a prescribed budget or stability criterion and return \(\theta_k\), together with a fresh simulation estimate of its objective value.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Logarithmically cooled stochastic-approximation annealing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded continuous- and discrete-time Langevin annealing schedules; the extract does not enumerate all regularity and stability hypotheses used by the cited convergence analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The annealed diffusion is
\[
dX_t=-\nabla f(X_t)\,dt+\eta(t)\,dW_t,
\qquad \eta(t)=\sqrt{\frac{C}{\log t}},\quad C>\Lambda(f),
\]
and merely requiring \(\eta(t)=o(1)\) is insufficient. Its discrete-time counterpart is
\[
x_{n+1}=x_n+a(n)[-\nabla f(x_n)+M_{n+1}]+b(n)W_{n+1},
\]
with
\[
a(n)=\frac{A}{n},\qquad b(n)=\sqrt{\frac{B}{n\log\log n}},\qquad n\ge2.
\]
Under the standing regularity, stability, and noise hypotheses of the referenced analysis, which are not specified in this extract, the threshold condition \(B/A>C\) yields convergence in probability to the global-minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method combines stochastic approximation with deliberately added Gaussian noise that cools logarithmically. Noise tending merely to zero is not enough. With the displayed continuous-time and discrete-time schedules, the stated threshold conditions, and the omitted standing hypotheses of the referenced analysis, the discrete iterates converge in probability to the global-minimizer set.
assumptions_latex: A,B,C>0
C>\Lambda(f)
a(n)=A/n
b(n)=\sqrt{B/(n\log\log n)},\quad n\ge2
B/A>C
\{M_n\}\text{ is martingale-difference measurement noise}
\{W_n\}\text{ is i.i.d. }N(0,I)
\text{The referenced analysis's additional regularity and stability assumptions hold}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}\!\left(x_n,\operatorname{Argmin}f\right)\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0.

children.title: Annealing Global-Convergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes associated with global rather than merely local annealing behavior.

assumptions_latex: The state space \(S\) is finite and the proposal kernel is irreducible and reversible with positive probabilities on its neighborhood edges.
The objective \(f:S\to\mathbb R\) is observed exactly, and \(D^*\) denotes the maximal energy barrier separating a nonoptimal state from lower-energy states.
The temperature is \(T_k=c/\log(k+2)\) with \(c>D^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(S^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S}f(x)\), the annealing chain satisfies \(\mathbb P(X_k\in S^*)\to1\).

notation.meaning: critical depth of the objective landscape under the proposal graph

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite-state logarithmic-cooling convergence in probability for exact Metropolis annealing.

source_refs.locator: 1.5.2 Simulated annealing p. 48

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((X_k)\) be the inhomogeneous Metropolis chain for minimizing \(f\), with acceptance probability \(\min\{1,\exp(-(f(y)-f(x))/T_k)\}\) for a proposed move from \(x\) to \(y\). If the logarithmic cooling constant exceeds the landscape critical depth, then
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}\mathbb P\!\left(X_k\in S^*\right)=1,
\qquad S^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S}f(x).
\]
Thus logarithmic cooling above the barrier threshold gives global convergence in probability. The assertion does not imply eventual absorption at a single minimizer, and faster schedules are not covered by this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite connected state space, logarithmic cooling slower than the critical barrier threshold drives exact annealing toward the global minimizers in probability.

children.title: Annealing Cooling-Schedule Families
children.top_down_role: Major temperature-decay families used in simulation-based annealing.

assumptions_latex: A cooling schedule is a deterministic sequence \((T_k)_{k\geq0}\) satisfying \(T_k>0\), \(T_{k+1}\leq T_k\), and \(T_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Logarithmic, polynomial, and geometric schedules are distinguished by their asymptotic decay rates and generally support different convergence guarantees.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard deterministic temperature families, classified by asymptotic cooling rate.

source_refs.locator: 1.5.2 Simulated annealing p. 48

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Three common cooling-schedule families are
\[
T_k=\frac{c}{\log(k+2)},\qquad T_k=\frac{T_0}{(k+1)^p},\qquad T_k=T_0r^k,
\]
where \(c>0\), \(T_0>0\), \(p>0\), and \(r\in(0,1)\). They are called logarithmic, polynomial, and geometric cooling, respectively. Their rates satisfy \(T_k^{\mathrm{geom}}=o(T_k^{\mathrm{poly}})\) and \(T_k^{\mathrm{poly}}=o(T_k^{\log})\) for fixed admissible parameters. A piecewise-constant schedule is specified by temperatures \(\tau_j\downarrow0\) and holding times \(h_j\), with \(T_k=\tau_j\) throughout stage \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cooling schedules commonly decrease logarithmically, polynomially, geometrically, or by temperature stages; these families cool at materially different asymptotic rates.
knowledge_statements.title: Annealing Cooling-Schedule Families

children.title: Annealing Noise-Cooling Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Relationships between simulation-error control and temperature decay.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), the estimated loss difference is \(\widehat\Delta_k=\Delta_k+E_k\), and \(E_k\) is conditionally sub-Gaussian with variance proxy \(2\sigma^2/n_k\).
A deterministic tolerance sequence satisfies \(\varepsilon_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed summability and scale conditions make simulation comparison errors asymptotically negligible relative to annealing.

notation.meaning: replications used in an iteration-k comparison

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient sub-Gaussian replication condition for noisy Metropolis comparisons.

source_refs.locator: 1.5.2 Simulated annealing p. 48
4 Simulation and sensitivity estimation p. 211

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A sufficient noise-cooling compatibility condition is
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\exp\left(-\frac{n_k\varepsilon_k^2}{4\sigma^2}\right)<\infty
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{\varepsilon_k}{T_k}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The sub-Gaussian tail bound then gives \(\sum_k\mathbb P(|E_k|>\varepsilon_k\mid\mathcal F_k)<\infty\), so comparison errors exceeding \(\varepsilon_k\) occur only finitely often almost surely under the conditional Borel--Cantelli criterion. The second condition makes the remaining error negligible in the Metropolis exponent. Consequently, replication counts must grow as temperature falls; fixed \(n_k\) generally does not satisfy this sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simulation effort must increase fast enough that large comparison errors are summable and residual errors are small relative to temperature.
knowledge_statements.title: Annealing Noise-Cooling Compatibility

source_witnesses.locator: 1.5.2 Simulated annealing p. 48
4 Simulation and sensitivity estimation p. 211

A locator for the exact compatibility result is needed.

children.title: Structured Discrete-Space Search Family
children.top_down_role: Search over graph-structured or recursively partitioned decision spaces.

children.title: Stochastic Discrete Local Search
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood exploration with uncertain comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Discrete Local Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood descent driven by sequential simulation comparisons, with distinct certified and budget-limited termination outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in S\). At iteration \(k\), select one or more candidates from \(N(x_k)\), allocate simulation replications to the incumbent and candidates, and apply a specified sequential comparison rule with controlled error probabilities. If a candidate \(y_k\) is declared better than \(x_k\), set \(x_{k+1}=y_k\); otherwise increase sampling, examine another neighbor, or retain \(x_k\) according to the declared policy. Stop either when every neighbor required by the policy has been tested and rejected as nonimproving or when a sampling or total-budget limit is reached. Return the incumbent, the comparison statistics, and a termination status distinguishing certified local termination from unresolved budget termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequentially simulate neighboring decisions and move to a statistically preferred neighbor. Report whether termination certifies that the required neighbors were nonimproving or merely records exhaustion of the sampling budget.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(S\) is finite or countable, and every \(x\in S\) has a finite neighborhood \(N(x)\).
Simulation output has finite mean \(f(x)\) for every feasible decision.
The comparison procedure terminates with a declared winner or an unresolved outcome at its prescribed sampling limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified local termination reports no improving neighbor under the adopted comparison rule; budget-limited termination makes no such certificate.

children.title: Nested Partitions
children.top_down_role: Adaptive partitioning of discrete decision spaces.

assumptions_latex: The discrete feasible set \(S\) admits recursive finite partitions.
Every sampled decision has an integrable simulation loss with mean \(f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm adaptively refines promising regions while retaining the ability to backtrack to their complements.

notation.meaning: children forming a partition of the current region

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic nested-partitions search on a recursively partitionable discrete space.

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Discrete Optimization p. 46

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with \(R_0=S\). At iteration \(k\), partition \(R_k\) into disjoint children \(R_{k,1},\ldots,R_{k,q_k}\), include \(S\setminus R_k\) as a surrounding region when nonempty, and sample feasible decisions from every candidate region. Estimate a prescribed region score, such as the smallest adequately sampled loss observed within that region. Select the region with the best score: descend to that child if it lies inside \(R_k\), or backtrack to the appropriate ancestor when the surrounding region wins. Update incumbent statistics, and stop at the partition-depth or simulation budget limit; return the best resampled decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively partition the current region, simulate candidates in its children and surrounding region, then descend or backtrack according to estimated promise.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Partitions

children.title: Statistical Branching Search System
